title: My Perfect Greek Vacation
subtitle: A travel booking concept that reduces choice overload and builds confidence before checkout.
coverAlt: My Perfect Greek Vacation concept cover

facts.label: focus
value: Decision clarity, confidence, and curated experience

value.text: Travel booking is increasingly a decision problem, not a search problem. Most platforms overwhelm users with inventory before they know what they actually want.
My Perfect Greek Vacation is a concept for a travel experience that shapes intent early, then surfaces options that feel meaningful and manageable.
Users struggle with too many destinations, inconsistent comparison, and unclear trade-offs. They often delay decisions or default to the safest option.

items: Lack of confidence in final choice

value.text: The concept had to work with existing travel inventory and still feel simpler. It could not rely on perfect data or heavy personalization on the first pass.

items: Requirement to support both mobile and desktop

value.text: Users do not want to choose from a catalogue. They want to narrow options through meaning, values, and practical confidence. The design must support that mental shift.
The core decision happens before users reach inventory. If the experience helps users articulate what matters, it can turn browsing into a confident selection process.
I designed a decision-first flow that captures user intent early, converts it into curated options, and explains why each choice fits.

items: Start with preference capture, not inventory
Limit visible options to reduce overload
Explain each recommendation with clear reasoning
Allow users to refine without losing progress
Decision layer first — help users define goals before showing options.
Curated option cards — show 3–5 meaningful offers instead of full inventory.
Reasoning labels — answer why this package matches the user.
Progressive refinement — let users adjust preferences without restarting.

value.caption: A diagram of the decision-first flow used to ground the travel concept in user intent and clarity.

value.text: The resulting concept is a travel experience that feels focused, understandable, and easy to choose. Users move from uncertainty to a clear vacation choice with fewer distractions.
The concept improves confidence by turning travel selection into a guided decision process rather than a chaotic browsing session. It can reduce abandonment and increase clarity in product messaging.

items: Better alignment between user goals and offers
